Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with right
knee pain and swelling. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the kind
and force of the impact observed. Initial examination revealed effusion and tenderness
along the medial joint line, with positive findings on the valgus stress test, while
other ligamentous and neurovascular assessments returned within normal limits. Imaging
was reviewed and did not show acute fracture. No prior injury to the right knee is
documented in the available history. Care was delivered over 18 visits consisting of
physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and activity modification. Treatment
followed a typical progression, with visit frequency tapering as range of motion and
pain improved. Billed services reflect the planned course of care, with no duplicate
or repeated charges identified. At last follow-up the patient was improving and was
discharged to a home exercise program with instructions to return if symptoms worsen.
